title: Adult-onset seizure + brain calcifications in an immigrant: neurocysticercosis
vignette: A 27-year-old man is brought to the hospital after having a generalized tonic-clonic seizure an hour ago. The patient has no chronic medical conditions and takes no medication. He emigrated from Nicaragua to the United States 5 years ago. Vital signs are within normal limits. Complete neurologic examination reveals no abnormalities. A CT scan of the head is shown in the image below: the scan shows multiple small calcified nodules in the brain parenchyma. Complete blood count and cerebrospinal fluid evaluation are within normal limits. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

clues.note: New-onset (adult) seizure is the most common presentation of intraparenchymal neurocysticercosis.
Neurocysticercosis is common in rural developing regions (Central/South America, sub-Saharan Africa, Asia) with free-roaming pigs and poor sanitation.

clues.text: multiple small calcified nodules in the brain parenchyma
clues.note: Multiple small calcified brain nodules represent nonviable (dead) cysts - the classic imaging of neurocysticercosis; viable cysts are round and hypodense +/- a scolex.

whatMatters: Adult-onset seizure + MULTIPLE CALCIFIED brain nodules in an immigrant from an endemic region (with normal CBC/CSF) = NEUROCYSTICERCOSIS from Taenia solium (pork tapeworm) egg ingestion. Answer C.
strategy: Combine epidemiology (endemic-region immigrant), presentation (adult-onset seizure, normal exam/CSF), and imaging (multiple calcified cysts, sometimes with a scolex) to reach neurocysticercosis. Reject cryptococcosis (AIDS, elevated CSF pressure/low glucose, hydrocephalus - not calcifications), miliary TB/tuberculoma (CSF lymphocytic pleocytosis, high protein, ring-enhancing lesions), neurosyphilis (CSF pleocytosis, tabes/paresis - seizures uncommon), and toxoplasmosis (AIDS, ring-enhancing lesions with fever).

eliminations.label: Cryptococcosis - AIDS, abnormal CSF
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: cryptococcal meningitis (a yeast, common in AIDS). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it causes subacute meningitis with increased CSF pressure and low glucose (and hydrocephalus on imaging), not multiple calcified parenchymal nodules with normal CSF. ✅ Correct if: AIDS with headache and India-ink/antigen-positive CSF.

eliminations.label: Miliary TB / tuberculoma - abnormal CSF, ring-enhancing
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: CNS tuberculosis forming tuberculomas. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: CSF typically shows lymphocytic pleocytosis and high protein, and lesions are ring-enhancing, unlike this normal CSF with calcified nodules. ✅ Correct if: CNS TB with abnormal CSF and ring-enhancing lesions.

eliminations.label: Neurosyphilis - CSF pleocytosis, seizures uncommon
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: CNS syphilis (meningovascular, tabes dorsalis, general paresis). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: seizures are uncommon and CSF usually shows lymphocytic pleocytosis/high protein; imaging isn't calcified cysts. ✅ Correct if: tabes dorsalis/general paresis with reactive CSF serology.

eliminations.label: Toxoplasmosis - AIDS, ring-enhancing + fever
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: cerebral toxoplasmosis (reactivation in AIDS). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it shows ring-enhancing lesions (often basal ganglia) with fever in immunosuppressed patients, not multiple calcifications with normal CBC/CSF. ✅ Correct if: AIDS (CD4 <100) with ring-enhancing brain lesions.

reasoning: Adult-onset seizure with an otherwise normal exam and normal CBC/CSF
CT shows multiple small calcified parenchymal nodules (nonviable cysts)
mechanism: NEUROCYSTICERCOSIS is caused by infection with the larval form of TAENIA SOLIUM (pork tapeworm) after ingestion of its EGGS in fecally contaminated food/water (fecal-oral). It is common in rural developing regions where pigs roam in human waste. Ingested eggs hatch in the small intestine, and larvae disseminate to tissues - brain, muscle, subcutaneous tissue, eyes - forming CYSTS. CNS disease most often presents with ADULT-ONSET SEIZURES from an intraparenchymal cyst, typically MONTHS TO YEARS after infection as cysts degenerate; examination, blood counts, and CSF are frequently NORMAL. Neuroimaging reveals >=1 cysts in varying stages: VIABLE cysts are round and hypodense (sometimes with a visible SCOLEX, which is pathognomonic), DEGENERATING cysts enhance with surrounding edema, and NONVIABLE cysts appear as small CALCIFIED nodules (as here). The distractors are other CNS infections with different CSF/imaging: cryptococcosis and toxoplasmosis (AIDS-associated), CNS tuberculosis (tuberculoma), and neurosyphilis.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Micro > neurocysticercosis: Taenia solium egg ingestion (fecal-oral); adult-onset seizure; cysts in brain (viable = hypodense +/- scolex; nonviable = calcified); normal CSF often; treat albendazole +/- steroids (+ antiepileptics).

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Immigrant + adult seizure + calcified brain cysts + normal CSF = neurocysticercosis.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on neurocysticercosis, Taenia solium, cysticercosis vs taeniasis, scolex, or ring-enhancing lesions? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Cryptococcus/Toxoplasma = AIDS (abnormal CSF/ring-enhancing); TB = pleocytosis/tuberculoma; neurosyphilis = reactive CSF.

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.text: CT head (stem): multiple small CALCIFIED parenchymal nodules = nonviable cysts of neurocysticercosis (not ring-enhancing or hydrocephalus).

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: adult-onset seizure + calcified brain cysts + endemic exposure = neurocysticercosis (Taenia solium).

firstAid.detail: Micro: T solium eggs; adult seizure; calcified brain cysts.
Micro > cryptococcus/toxo (AIDS), TB, neurosyphilis differ by CSF/imaging.
Micro > pork larvae -> adult worm; egg ingestion -> cysticercosis.

memoryHook: Young immigrant, first-ever seizure, and the CT is dotted with little calcified stones - old pork-tapeworm cysts: neurocysticercosis.
